title: She Makes $2K Every Saturday From Her Parents' Front Porch
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast

stated_problem.quote: I just wanted a different way to sell and a way to sell more often and just something unique and fun
stated_problem.speaker: Angela

idea.name: Saturday porch bakery
idea.one_liner: Bake and sell bread, pastries and other baked goods to local customers through Saturday porch pickup and pre-orders.
idea.customer: Nearby consumers who want fresh baked goods.
idea.offer: Home-baked goods sold from a porch cart, with walk-up purchases and pre-orders.
idea.revenue_model: Direct product sales and pre-paid online orders.

key_quotes.quote: Yeah, so I have a home bakery that I run out of my house.
And every single Saturday, I roll out this cart and I stock it full of goodies and people just come and purchase.
And so I just wanted a different way to sell and a way to sell more often and just something unique and fun and so I saw something like this on social media.
I know I use Next Door. That was like my first really hit that I did with social media just cuz Next Door focuses a lot on the locals and people directly in your neighborhood.
So, I usually have to do like my online ingredient stock all after on Saturday. And so then that's when it all starts over.

claims.claim: Angela reports Saturday sales of about $2,000 to $2,100.
claims.quote: Recently, I've been doing about 2,000 to 2100 in sales on a Saturday.

claims.claim: The host frames the opportunity as making $2,000 in an hour on Saturday mornings.
claims.quote: What if you could make $2,000 in 1 hour every Saturday morning from your parents' [music] front porch?

claims.claim: The host describes Angela as making $2,000 in one hour every Saturday.
claims.quote: Angela, 20 years old, making $2,000 in 1 hour every Saturday morning with a micro bakery. She started 7 months ago.

claims.claim: The host estimates about 100 people in line.
claims.quote: So, we're talking like a hundred people, I would say.

claims.claim: Angela says she bought the cart building plan for about $15 on Etsy.
claims.quote: So, I bought a building plan. It was like 15 bucks off of Etsy.

claims.quote: So, 12 bucks for sourdough, cinnamon rolls.

claims.quote: I usually do So, I'll do some singles, which I'll do five for a single and then 15 for a three-pack.

claims.quote: And then I have cake slices, which that one I started at seven. I up to eight because butter is so expensive.

claims.claim: Angela charges $5 for a large cookie.
claims.quote: So I'll do five for those. Five bucks for a cookie.

claims.claim: Angela charges $9 for a four-pack of bagels.
claims.quote: Bagels, I do fourpack for $9.

claims.claim: Angela charges $8 for a four-pack of English muffins.
claims.quote: English muffins, I'll do four pack for eight.

claims.claim: Angela says Saturday sales are about $2,000 to $21,100; the transcript's figure is inconsistent with her other estimate.
claims.quote: Recently, I've been doing about 2,000 to 21,100 in sales on a Saturday.

claims.claim: Ingredients cost about $300 per week and packaging about $100 per week.
claims.quote: And then usually my ingredients is about 300 per week. Packaging is about a hundred.

claims.claim: Angela estimates about $500 for the costs she is discussing; the precise breakdown is unclear.
claims.quote: I would say about 500 for that.

claims.claim: Angela pays herself about $800 per week.
claims.quote: And then I pay myself about $800 per week.

claims.claim: The host restates the business as $2,000 revenue with $500 in hard costs.
claims.quote: So call it on a Saturday morning $2,000 revenue. 500 of that in hard cost packaging and ingredients.

claims.quote: Usually, I'll for the walkups I've been selling out by 9, which is amazing.

claims.quote: And so, usually I've had people message me like as soon as it opens cuz I think I have about 800 people waiting to pre once, which is a lot.

claims.claim: Angela says most pre-order customers are within 15 to 20 minutes away, with Rock Wall the furthest she recalls.
claims.quote: I would say most of them are probably within 15 to 20 minutes, but I think the furthest has been Rock Wall.

claims.claim: The host suggests that if 70% of orders came from a neighborhood 20 minutes away, another location might be worth trying.
claims.quote: Not that you're looking to like scale and you like take over the world, but if you saw for whatever reason 70% of my pre-order come from 20 minutes away this neighborhood, like maybe it'd be worth trying to add another location to that neighborhood.

claims.claim: Angela charges $12 for a classic sourdough loaf and $13 to $14 for specialty loaves.
claims.quote: Usually my classic loaf I'll do 12. And then my specialty ones, it ranges from 13 to 14.

claims.claim: Angela says her classic loaf had previously been $11 before she raised it to $12.

claims.quote: So how much was that? It was about 10,000.

claims.quote: So if you have a $1,500 profit morning, right? Just hard cost of 500.

claims.quote: Maybe 3,000. And, you know, see where that goes. Um, but you need to hire someone.

claims.quote: And so, I'll hire her for like 30 minutes. And so, I track that, you know, cuz I'll pay her.

claims.quote: You pay them like 12 bucks a month per employee.

claims.quote: I mean, 2 to 3,000 a week, 52 weeks, you could gross over 100 grand this year.

claims.claim: Angela says the certification lasts about three years.
claims.quote: I think it lasts like 3 years.

claims.claim: The host describes the neighborhood as having about 250 homes and 1,000 people.
claims.quote: I think it's relevant to note that there's like 250 homes in your neighborhood, right? That's like a thousand people, right?

claims.quote: If if someone goes to a farmers market a half hour away and they see sourdough for 12 bucks, they probably won't buy. But because of the fact that they they live near you and they have an affinity to you and they're following you on social media, like they'd probably pay 15, you know, like there is a correlation there.

claims.claim: Angela says a farmers-market stall cost about $180 for one day.
claims.quote: For me, it was about 180 and that's for one day if you sourdough.

claims.claim: Angela says her highest farmers-market sales were $550.
claims.quote: My highest selling one was 550.

claims.claim: The host estimates that farmers-market profit may have been about $100 to $200, and Angela agrees.
claims.quote: So you you're scraping out a 100 maybe 200 maybe. Yeah.

acquisition_channels.details: Angela posted behind-the-scenes videos and a TikTok POV video that brought local attention; she also recommends posting on social media.
She used Nextdoor and recommends local Facebook groups.
She recommends word of mouth through family and friends.
Walk-up sales from the porch cart, with a sign pointing customers to the house.
She tried a local farmers market; she reports a high stall fee and lower returns than the porch.

ideas.delivery: Angela bakes at home, mainly on Fridays with some items made Saturday morning, then stocks and attends the porch cart, restocking and helping walk-up customers. Pre-orders are paid online through Hot Plate and set out for pickup; she sometimes pays family or a friend to help.
ideas.other_uk_rules: A UK version should check local-authority food-business registration, food hygiene, allergen and labelling requirements; UK GDPR applies to customer data collected for pre-orders. The transcript describes Texas cottage-food rules, which do not transfer to the UK.
